fatal_errors: The proposed MoS2-polymer composite does not reconstruct the CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 high-entropy-alloy composite or the intervention of varying Mo content.
No polymer is identified, so thermal stability, mechanical strength, processing, and applicability above 300 °C cannot be assessed; many polymers degrade or soften severely in this regime.

The hypothesis omits the Ag, Cr2O3, Ni-coated MoS2, Mo-induced lattice distortion, sigma-phase strengthening, and high-temperature silver-molybdate glaze that are central to the target material's performance.
No cited evidence supports the claimed elevated-temperature performance.
explanation: The response recognizes MoS2 as a solid lubricant and proposes a comparative friction-and-wear test, giving it limited alignment with the broad self-lubrication problem. However, it replaces the target SPS-fabricated high-entropy-alloy composite with an unspecified polymer composite and provides no matching composition, processing conditions, temperature-resolved behavior, strengthening mechanism, or tribochemical mechanism. Its proposed baseline and falsification rule are conceptually usable but too underspecified to establish wide-temperature performance, and the absence of evidence is especially serious given the questionable stability of an unspecified polymer above 300 °C.
